summary: Pier light at the Pentwater River harbour: a wooden tower lit in 1873, a 1890 range post, and the 1937 and 1987 towers that mark the entrance today.

structures.note: Square tower at outer end of south pier; LighthouseFriends says the tower was later given to a yacht club

access.note: LighthouseFriends gives directions to Charles Mears State Park for viewing the lights.

events.note: Square open-frame wooden tower at the outer end of the south pier
Fixed red light first placed in operation on 20 June 1873
Schooner Mercury ashore near Pentwater in a gale and snowstorm on the evening of 20 November 1879 (the 1880 report dates the entry to 20 November); not tied to the light
Tubular-lantern post at the outer end of the south pier forming a range with the pierhead light; first lit 15 August 1890
Elevated walk 500 feet long and 10 feet high built at the Pentwater pierhead range (Light-House Board, FY ended 30 June 1900)
Severe storm of 8-10 November 1913 damaged the Pentwater Pierhead Range; five stations together about $6,500
Front and rear lights changed from oil to acetylene; keeper position eliminated; elevated walk removed (LighthouseFriends)
Metal skeletal tower placed on the south pier in June
Old wooden tower acquired for mounting on a yacht club clubhouse roof
Prefabricated cylindrical tower placed on the north pier on 8 October 1987; carries a light, foghorn and radiobeacon

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27. Changes made: (a) the Mercury wreck is dated 20 November 1879 from the 1880 report (scan pages 96-97), replacing 'no month in the excerpt'; (b) the story said neither storm event touched the light, but the 1913 damage was to the Pentwater Pierhead Range, so the text now says so; (c) LighthouseFriends says the yacht club commodore enlisted help 'in gaining ownership', not that the club won it; the text now says that; (d) the Army Corps 'finished replacing' the piers in 1937; (e) the Mears channel sentence is now sourced, and 'the harbour grew out of lumber' was removed as an unsourced summary; (f) only one LighthouseFriends quotation remains ('the position of keeper was eliminated'); 'lengthy service' is paraphrased. Still open: (1) Keeper disagreement: the archive roster starts with John Davenport in 1873 and gives Francis McGuire 1873 to 1877; LighthouseFriends names McGuire as first keeper. Both are stated; the roster lines carry person slugs. (2) Current status: no Coast Guard List of Lights entry was checked, so the story does not say the light is lit. (3) The 1900 Light-House Board entry is cited by scan page 166; its printed page was not read. The archive index lists Pentwater at page 140. (4) The 1879/1880 Mercury episode is a Pentwater event in the Life-Saving Service reports, not an event at the light; it is kept as context. Check whether the editor wants it, given the station brief. (5) Two targeted Chronicling America searches for Pentwater light keepers returned nothing usable. (6) No photos were supplied or found. (7) The record says the 1873 wooden tower is standing; the story does not repeat that claim (see corrections). (8) Oceana County is from the station record, not from a source read here.
